failure_summary.description: Agents imported a nonexistent tools module instead of calling the injected functions directly.
Agents omitted required filters or failed to save newly generated results.
An accepted suggestion for a new attraction category was treated as requiring no planning.
A route and both round-trip dates already present in the conversation were incorrectly treated as missing.
An already available, compatible restaurant result was searched again without a new criterion.
A standardized flight-class value was title-cased instead of using the tool's expected lowercase value.

patch.reasoning: Most failures violate instructions already stated in the skill, so repeating those rules would not patch a gap. The flight-class mismatch reveals a narrower ambiguity: preserving user-provided casing for entities should not lead to changing the canonical casing of standardized tool options.

edits.target: - Match arguments only to fields declared by the selected tool’s schema, with the expected type and cardinality. Never pass a preference as an unsupported extra argument or place it in an unrelated field. For range-shaped fields, encode an explicitly exact value as both endpoints (for example, `[n, n]`); encode a minimum rating or a request for at least or better as `[n, schema_max]`. Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`). For attraction searches, use each explicitly provided location field (`city` and/or `state`) in the matching schema field along with the requested category or name. A state alone is usable when the tool supports state-level search; do not ask for a city when it does.
